concepts.label: CRUD Operations (insert/get/replace/remove via Collection API, with Options classes)
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - 'The core interface to Couchbase Server is simple KV operations on full documents' matches the promoted definition exactly. Python's *Options()-class-plus-keyword-override pattern (InsertOptions(), GetOptions(), etc.) is a different configuration idiom from Java's builder style, but the underlying operation set (insert/get/replace/remove/upsert) is identical.

concepts.label: CAS (Compare-And-Swap) Optimistic Locking
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - matches the Java SDK's extraction-layer sdk:cas-optimistic-locking exactly; Python's CAS section ('a value representing the current state of an item; each time the item is modified, its CAS changes') describes the identical mechanism, including the same get-modify-replace-with-cas pattern.

concepts.label: Durability Options (ServerDurability levels; ClientDurability/observe-based fallback)
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - matches the Java SDK's extraction-layer sdk:durability ('client-library option wrapping a server durability feature'). Python additionally documents, on this same page, the pre-6.5 legacy 'client verified'/observe-based ClientDurability(ReplicateTo, PersistTo) fallback alongside the newer ServerDurability enum - both are the SDK-side durability OPTION, so both fall under this one id rather than needing a second concept.

concepts.label: Document Expiration / TTL (expiry, touch, get_and_touch)
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - matches Java's sdk:document-expiration; Python's Touch/get_and_touch operations are the same mechanism under the same names.

concepts.label: Atomic Counters (binary().increment()/.decrement())
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - matches Java's sdk:atomic-counters; Python's collection.binary().increment/decrement with IncrementOptions/DecrementOptions(delta=...) describes the identical counter-document mechanism, including the same 'seed with an initial value' pattern and the same XDCR atomicity caveat.

concepts.label: KV Range Scan (RangeScan, PrefixScan, SamplingScan)
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - matches Java's sdk:kv-range-scan ('KV Range Scan (rangeScan, prefixScan, samplingScan)') exactly, down to the same three scan-kind names (RangeScan/PrefixScan/SamplingScan vs Java's rangeScan/prefixScan/samplingScan) and the identical 'use SQL++ instead for low-latency/high-concurrency' framing.

concepts.label: Preferred Server Group Replica Reads
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - a Server-Group-aware read-routing feature (SDK 4.4.0+, Server 7.6.2+) with no equivalent concept in the registry excerpt supplied for this round; it is a replica-read/locality optimization, not a durability or KV-CRUD concept, so it doesn't fit any existing sdk:* id.

notable_absence.finding: The CAUTION box states setting three replicas on a bucket 'disables durability for sync writes ... also precluding the use of multi-document ACID transactions' - a genuine mutual-exclusion fact between a bucket-topology setting and sdk:distributed-transaction. Not modeled as a relation because the subject side (a specific replica-count bucket configuration) has no registry concept of its own; capturing it would require minting a narrow bucket-config concept purely to hold one caveat, so it's flagged in prose (and repeated verbatim in this batch's data-durability-acid-transactions.json) instead.

cross_component_finding: This page duplicates, word-for-word, the entire 'Preferred Server Group Replica Reads' section (including the CAUTION box) found on concept-docs/data-durability-acid-transactions.md in this same batch - a structural content-duplication pattern (same prose block reused across a howto and its concept-doc sibling) rather than two independently-authored descriptions of the same feature.
cross_product_finding: Strong reuse signal across five of Java's extraction-layer sdk:* ids in one page (kv-operations, cas-optimistic-locking, durability, document-expiration, atomic-counters, kv-range-scan) - Python's howto is structured almost identically to what the Java-derived labels describe, operation-name-for-operation-name (RangeScan/PrefixScan/SamplingScan vs Java's rangeScan/prefixScan/samplingScan; ServerDurability(Durability.MAJORITY) vs Java's DurabilityLevel enum). The one genuinely new mint, sdk:preferred-server-group-replica-reads, is NOT a rejected-Java-reuse case - it's a feature with no corresponding entry anywhere in the round's supplied registry excerpt, so it reads as either Python-specific novelty or (more likely) a feature the Java-SDK batches simply didn't cover in their chosen page set. Notably, Python documents BOTH the modern ServerDurability enum AND the legacy pre-6.5 ClientDurability(ReplicateTo, PersistTo) 'observe-based' fallback on the very same page under the same sdk:durability concept - if Java's sdk:durability extraction covered only the modern enum, this page shows the same id needs to stretch to cover a second, older API shape too.
